title: Drones and the role of batteries in modern defence
gist: Defence is described as a small but fast-growing driver of battery demand, led by drones, with Benchmark's automotive research lead flagging shifting drone battery chemistries and China's continued role in Western drone supply chains.

themes.theme: Defence as an Emerging Battery Demand Driver

insights.claim: Defence applications are a small but fast-growing driver of battery demand, with drones identified as the leading source of that growth.
insights.speaker: Will Roberts, automotive research lead, Benchmark; Bryan Bille, lead policy and geopolitics analyst, Benchmark
insights.so_what: Investors mapping battery demand beyond EVs and grid storage should start tracking defence/drone procurement as an incremental, fast-growing demand pool worth sizing separately.
insights.quote: Defence is a small but fast-growing battery demand driver, with drones leading it.

insights.claim: Battery chemistry choices used in military and commercial drones are shifting, and China continues to play a role in Western drone battery supply chains despite the defence/geopolitical sensitivity of the sector.
insights.speaker: Will Roberts, automotive research lead, Benchmark; Bryan Bille, lead policy and geopolitics analyst, Benchmark
insights.so_what: A continued Chinese footprint in Western drone battery supply chains, even in a defence-sensitive category, points to a supply-chain de-risking gap that Western drone and battery manufacturers may need to close.
insights.locator: Will Roberts explains the changing chemistry trends for drones and role of China in Western supply chains

source_meta.author: Will Roberts, automotive research lead, Benchmark; Bryan Bille, lead policy and geopolitics analyst, Benchmark
